scope: Reversible opt-in DEV15.8 same-area light diagnostic and labelled private report flow; not an FPS fix or full art/animation review.
findings: Seven original final-package captures inspected: Chromium and Apple WebKit start/result panels, both report-control panels, and ordinary WebKit new-game surface.
Diagnostic text and action buttons are readable and fit within the tested landscape view. Results show all seven stages, restored state, SEND REPORT and CLOSE without clipping.
Starting and restored views retain the game environment, hero and pet. No new diagnostic visual corruption observed.
Source review confirms sample flush before light-state mutation, interval reset at stage boundaries, pending report protection, and restoration on focus, movement, menu/area or recorder interruption.
Final evidence passes ordinary recording/mining, browser reload recovery, exact labelled transfer, receipt clearing, isolation of each light category and cancellation in each off state.
Publisher review confirms immutable original export and validation provenance, evidence hashes, exact candidate bytes, LIVE/Worn preservation and post-publication byte checks.
nonblocking_notes: send() normalizes report.reason to stopped; explicit lighttest:end:complete or lighttest:end:cancelled markers preserve diagnostic outcome.
The diagnostic overlay intentionally covers parts of the existing HUD while requiring the player to stand still.
limitations: Mac Chromium and Apple WebKit evidence does not prove physical iPhone FPS, thermal behavior or Safari app lifecycle.
Chromium completes the production 180-second sequence; WebKit QA accelerates production transitions, so its displayed 20-second result is functional evidence only.
Browser sender/receipt assertions use a transfer fixture. Existing receiver schema roundtrip remains a separate publisher gate.
Static captures do not establish animation smoothness; no 10/10 FPS score is assigned.
